name: Get agent readiness summary
description: Get agent readiness summary Returns a summary of AI agent readiness scores across scanned domains, grouped by the specified dimension. GET /client/v4/radar/agent_readiness/summary/{dimension}
context:
GET /client/v4/radar/agent_readiness/summary/{dimension}
Returns a summary of AI agent readiness scores across scanned domains, grouped by the specified dimension. Data is sourced from weekly bulk scans. All values are raw domain counts.
Required: dimension (path) — Specifies the agent readiness data dimension by which to group the results.
Optional: date (query) — Filters results by the specified date.; domainCategory (query) — Filters results by domain category.; name (query) — Array of names used to label the series in the response.; format (query) — Format in which results will be returned.

name: Get Geolocation details
description: Get Geolocation details Retrieves the requested Geolocation information. GET /client/v4/radar/geolocations/{geo_id}
context:
GET /client/v4/radar/geolocations/{geo_id}
Retrieves the requested Geolocation information. Geolocation names can be localized by sending an `Accept-Language` HTTP header with a BCP 47 language tag (e.g., `Accept-Language: pt-PT`). The full quality-value chain is supported (e.g., `pt-PT,pt;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`).
Required: geo_id (path) — Geolocation ID. Refer to [GeoNames](https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/readme.txt)
Optional: format (query) — Format in which results will be returned.

name: List Geolocations
description: List Geolocations Retrieves a list of geolocations. GET /client/v4/radar/geolocations
context:
GET /client/v4/radar/geolocations
Retrieves a list of geolocations. Geolocation names can be localized by sending an `Accept-Language` HTTP header with a BCP 47 language tag (e.g., `Accept-Language: pt-PT`). The full quality-value chain is supported (e.g., `pt-PT,pt;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`).
Optional: limit (query) — Limits the number of objects returned in the response.; offset (query) — Skips the specified number of objects before fetching the results.; geoId (query) — Filters results by geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs.; location (query) — Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 location codes.; format (query) — Format in which results will be returned.

name: Search for locations, ASes, reports, and more
description: Search for locations, ASes, reports, and more Searches for locations, autonomous systems, reports, bots, certificate logs, certificate authorities, industries and verticals. GET /client/v4/radar/search/global
context:
GET /client/v4/radar/search/global
Searches for locations, autonomous systems, reports, bots, certificate logs, certificate authorities, industries and verticals. Location names can be localized by sending an `Accept-Language` HTTP header with a BCP 47 language tag (e.g., `Accept-Language: pt-PT`). The full quality-value chain is supported (e.g., `pt-PT,pt;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`).
Required: query (query) — String used to perform the search operation.
Optional: limit (query) — Limits the number of objects returned in the response.; limitPerGroup (query) — Limits the number of objects per search category.; include (query) — Search types included in results.; exclude (query) — Search types excluded from results.; format (query) — Format in which results will be returned.

name: Get TCP resets and timeouts summary
description: Get TCP resets and timeouts summary Retrieves the distribution of connection stage by TCP connections terminated within the first 10 packets by a reset or timeout. GET /client/v4/radar/tcp_resets_timeouts/summary
context:
GET /client/v4/radar/tcp_resets_timeouts/summary
Retrieves the distribution of connection stage by TCP connections terminated within the first 10 packets by a reset or timeout.
Optional: name (query) — Array of names used to label the series in the response.; dateRange (query) — Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).; dateStart (query) — Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.; dateEnd (query) — End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.; asn (query) — Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.; location (query) — Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.; continent (query) — Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.; format (query) — Format in which results will be returned.
